items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, decision block and the cost claim make the action clear: keep September, because both candidates cost more (+$0.62 and +$0.49 per 1,000 replies, paired and corrected) and neither holds character better. The main risk is missing from the first screen. Under the declared 15-point allowed loss, both candidates are acceptable on character (pass-rate drops of at most 10.8 and 5.8 points at 95%), so cost alone decides. But no provider is recorded for any arm, and the earlier round found qwen3.8-flash cheaper with high confidence. That conflict is tucked into the end of a margin Watch line about a rejected arm. It is not in the headline, the lede or the confidence line.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: The claims follow in order: cost decides, character does not rescue either candidate, off-lane asks carry most of the character loss, and the control fails there too. Each sentence matches its block row by row. The off-lane loss shares (48% and 53%), the off-lane failure counts (39, 64 and 62 trials) and the missing-cost bound in Method ($2.24 and $2.36 against $2.02) all check against the data. One small mismatch: Watch puts qwen3.8-flash's weakest margin at -12.6, 2.4 points inside, using the corrected interval. The 'What you could change' table puts its flip at 10.8, using the declared 95% reading.

items.name: Honest emphasis

Yet it rests on a provider routing the run never recorded, and the earlier round said the opposite for qwen3.8-flash. If routing put a candidate at or below $1.89, the call could flip, because both candidates sit inside the allowed loss.

items.reason: The cost forest shows the paired gaps and their intervals. The character forest marks the allowed loss. The off-lane bars show the slice changes the loss shares come from. Two smaller problems. The cost block's paired gaps (+$0.62 and +$0.49) differ from the gaps between the options table's means ($0.54 and $0.52) with no note on why. And the examples caption sets the candidates' failures against the control's 'customer-service refusal', but two of the three kept September off-lane failures also answer a non-music ask.

findings.finding: The confidence reads High, and its clauses say cost decides and 'does not rest on the judge'. But the cost order rests on a provider routing that was never recorded for any arm, and the earlier round found qwen3.8-flash cheaper with high confidence. Both candidates are inside the 15-point allowed loss (at most 10.8 and 5.8 points), so if routing put either at or below September's $1.89, the call could flip. Add a confidence clause for unrecorded routing: what would make it matter (a recorded routing where a candidate costs no more) and why the call holds until then. Qualify the headline and lede to say the costs are at this run's unrecorded routing. Move the conflict with the earlier round out of the margin Watch line into its own Watch item. If the analyst cannot stand behind that, lower the confidence.

The claim ranks the three models by cost with no provider named. The caption and Method do say no provider was recorded, but the claim sentence and the lede rank the models as if the gap were the models' own. Say in the claim sentence that the gap is at an unrecorded routing, so it may belong to the routing rather than the model, and point to the re-pricing next step.

This claim reads 1017's loss on holding character (-4.7 points, corrected), which carries the reasoning-share confound (55% against 76% for September). Neither the claim nor the confidence line carries it. Add the reasoning-ratio caveat to the claim.

The model-confound clause ('each arm's recorded settings name only its model') understates what the page itself shows. 1017's reasoning share differed (55% against 76%), and the simulator's request settings went unrecorded. Reword the clause so it acknowledges both, or point it to the reasoning-share Watch item and the Method note.

Watch gives qwen3.8-flash's weakest margin as the corrected interval reaching -12.6, 2.4 points inside -15. The 'What you could change' table and the declared reading put its flip at 10.8, from the 95% interval. Use one basis in both places, or say which each uses. Also drop the '+' from '+5.8 points' and '+10.8': they are allowed losses, not gains.

The lede and the cost block give paired gaps of +$0.62 and +$0.49, but the options table's means ($2.43 and $2.41 against $1.89) imply $0.54 and $0.52. The two differ because some trials report no cost and only matched cases are paired. Add a short note to the caption so a reader doesn't take the figures for a mistake.

The caption sets the candidates' failures (answering a question the persona should decline) against September's 'customer-service refusal'. But two of September's three kept off-lane failures (the landlord email and the laundry question) also answer a non-music ask. The cards are also only 3 of 39, 64 and 62 failures. Say they are a sample, and don't imply the control fails differently when its kept failures mostly fail the same way.

Method, cost basis: 'had its own missing trials cost its p95 ($2.02 per 1,000 replies)' reads as if September's p95 were $2.02. September's p95 is $5.30 per 1,000 replies, and $2.02 is its mean if its 33 missing trials cost that p95. Reword it, for example: 'had its missing trials each cost its p95 of $5.30, its mean would be $2.02, still below the candidates' floors of $2.24 and $2.36'.

findings.finding: Claim character uses 'holds character' for the pass rate on character adherence. It then says 1017 is 'down 3, not told apart'. But the judged check 'persona holds character' sits in the same block, and there 1017 is -4.7 points (-8.2 to -1.3 at 99.69%), separated and worse, as that block's own caption says. A reader takes the two for one measure, and the sentence then contradicts its own block. Fix: call the 7.6 and 3.0 figures 'the pass rate on character adherence'. Add a sentence on the judged holding-character check: both candidates are separated and worse, qwen3.8-flash -6.0 and 1017 -4.7. The confidence reads High over the unrecorded-routing caveat. That caveat is plausibly material: the page says cost alone decides, and that the earlier round found qwen3.8-flash cheaper. Its clause also contradicts itself, calling this run's gap 'the only cost evidence' while citing that earlier finding. Fix: scope the High to the character readings and to the cost order at this run's routing. Then say it leaves open whether a candidate costs less at a recorded production routing, which the earlier round suggests it may. Otherwise, make the form low.

The first next step says that if a candidate costs no more than September after re-pricing, 'then character decides'. The routing caveat says the call 'would turn on character alone or become a trade'. Under the declared criteria, a cheaper candidate inside the 15-point allowed loss would be the pick: qwen3.8-flash's worst corrected drop is -12.6, and 1017's is -7.4. Say so. If the team would not accept qwen3.8-flash's 7.6-point pass-rate drop at any price, say the allowed loss should be tightened now (qwen3.8-flash stops counting as acceptable below 10.8, 1017 below 5.8). Then a reader knows what a cheaper re-pricing would actually do to the call.
